rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Rana tigrina is the model amphibian for NEB. It is semi-aquatic, living near water but spending most of the time on land. Its external features — moist, glandular, scaleless skin; a tympanum; a nictitating membrane; 4-digit forelimbs and 5-digit webbed hindlimbs — reflect its amphibious life. The tadpole has a tail and gills; the adult loses the tail and gains lungs.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
External: head (eyes, tympanum, nostrils) + neck + trunk + 4 limbs (forelimb 4 digits, hindlimb 5 digits, webbed)
Adaptations: moist skin, webbed feet, sticky pads, tympanum, nictitating membrane
Metamorphosis: tadpole (tail + gills) → adult frog (no tail + lungs)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Frogs are amphibians (cold-blooded, moist skin, larval gills), NOT reptiles (dry scaly skin, lungs only).  ·  Adult frogs have NO tail; the tadpole larva has a tail (metamorphosis removes it).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects a labelled external diagram of the frog as the entry topic for frog anatomy.  ·  The digit count (4 forelimb, 5 hindlimb) is a very common exam detail.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Habitat: a frog sitting on a pond bank by day, entering water at night to feed and breed.  ·  External: webbed hind feet (swimming), sticky pads on forefeet (climbing), tympanum (hearing), nictitating membrane (eye protection).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The forelimbs have 4 digits and the hindlimbs have 5 webbed digits — a key exam detail.  ·  The tympanum is the external eardrum; the nictitating membrane is a transparent third eyelid for underwater vision.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Rana tigrina: amphibian, ~5–8 cm, semi-aquatic; model organism for NEB.  ·  External: moist glandular skin, tympanum, nictitating membrane.  ·  Forelimbs 4 digits; hindlimbs 5 webbed digits.  ·  No tail in adults; tadpole has a tail (metamorphosis).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Rana tigrina (the "tiger frog") is one of the largest common freshwater frogs in South Asia.  ·  The frog skin is so permeable that it can absorb both water and pollutants — the basis of its bio-indicator role.

rows.text: Metamorphosis: tadpole (tail + gills) → froglet → adult frog (lungs, no tail).  ·  Bio-indicator: frogs die off in polluted ponds, warning of water-quality decline.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Rana tigrina (tiger frog / Indian bullfrog): the model amphibian for NEB; ~5–8 cm long; found in ponds, streams, and wet grasslands.  ·  Habit and habitat: semi-aquatic; lives near water but spends most of the day on land; returns to water to breed; buries in moist soil in dry season.  ·  External features: moist, glandular, scaleless skin (mucus + colour glands); head with eyes, tympanum (eardrum), nostrils; distinct neck, trunk; 4-digit forelimbs, 5-digit webbed hindlimbs; nictitating membrane (third eyelid); tail absent in adults (present in tadpole).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Bio-indicator role  ·  Adaptations: webbed feet (swim), sticky pads (climb), moist skin (respiration).  ·  Taxonomy: Amphibia > Anura > Rana.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Bio-indicator of water quality; pest controller.  ·  Frogs breathe through lungs, moist skin (cutaneous), and the buccal cavity; tadpoles use gills.  ·  Rana tigrina lives in moist habitats; its permeable skin makes it a sensitive bio-indicator of water pollution.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Metamorphosis (tadpole → frog) is a frequent topic.  ·  Stress that the moist skin allows cutaneous respiration — a key amphibian feature.  ·  Note the frog as a water-quality bio-indicator (application question).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Memorise the digit count (4 fore, 5 hind).  ·  Learn the external features (tympanum, nictitating membrane, skin).  ·  List adaptations to amphibious life.
